oneLiner: The only proven non-NVIDIA inference architecture at scale: a $25.4B backlog and a cloud business that nearly quadrupled YoY, priced near 47x current-year core sales while GAAP still bleeds warrant amortization and IPO stock comp.
thesis: Genuine architectural differentiation: wafer-scale SRAM (WSE-3: ~900K cores, 44GB on-chip, ~21PB/s) keeps weights on-die; independent tests show 3-6x Groq's tokens/sec on identical open models.

Inference is becoming the dominant AI workload and speed/latency (agentic chains, reasoning models) is exactly where wafer-scale differentiates; Q2 confirmed the pivot - core cloud/services revenue (+287% YoY) overtook hardware.

Anchor validation: $10B multi-year OpenAI compute deal (750MW; launch partner for GPT-5.6 Sol at 750 tokens/sec); AWS Bedrock production set for Q1 2027; AMD disaggregated inference (up to 5x throughput, vendor figure) in production Q4 2026.

The bet is execution against a $25.4B RPO: management plans to more than triple revenue in 2027, needing 600MW+ of contracted data center capacity to land on time and manufacturing capacity to grow >10x in 2026.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 FY2026 (reported Aug 12, 2026 - after close)
points: Core revenue $209.9M, +103% YoY (GAAP $180.1M, +74%), beating the ~$194M guide; stock still fell ~17% after hours.
Mix flipped: core cloud/services $127.7M (+287%) overtook core hardware $82.1M (+17%); GAAP hardware fell ~23% to $54.1M after $28M of customer-warrant amortization.
Core gross margin 40.6% (+940bps YoY) vs GAAP 14.2%; core operating loss -$33.6M (-16% margin); GAAP net loss $450.5M (-$2.98/sh) on $377M of IPO-quarter stock comp.
RPO $25.4B as of Jun 30, 2026 - roughly 29x this year's guided core revenue.
Liquidity: $8.6B cash and short-term investments plus an $850M revolver; 1H26 operating cash flow -$47.5M, capex $549M.

segments: Cloud/inference services is now the larger and faster business: core cloud $127.7M (+287%) vs core hardware $82.1M (+17%) in Q2; hardware is lumpy, and customer-warrant amortization hits GAAP hardware revenue hardest.

Customer concentration still extreme: OpenAI, G42, MBZUAI, and AWS are named significant customers; FY2025 was 86% UAE entities. New logos (Cognition, Block, Figma, GSK, CrowdStrike) broaden the tail but not yet the core.
competitive: NVIDIA is the default and acquired Groq for $20B in Dec 2025 - a direct fast-inference response.
AMD went the other way: partnership integrating wafer-scale with Helios; disaggregated inference (claimed 5x throughput - vendor figure) in production Q4 2026.
Supply position is differentiated: no HBM, no CoWoS, no 3nm - the three chokepoints everyone else queues for.
Risk: commodity GPU token prices falling faster than the speed premium holds.
moat: Wafer-scale SRAM is hard to replicate and demonstrably fastest at inference today, but the moat is narrow: it depends on one TSMC process with no second source, and NVIDIA can buy or build fast-inference capability while bundling an unmatched software ecosystem. The $25.4B RPO is the strongest moat evidence yet - if it converts.
risks: Customer concentration: OpenAI (Master Relationship Agreement), G42, MBZUAI, and AWS dominate; the ramp deepens single-counterparty exposure.
Margin trough: Q3 guided sequentially worse (core GM 38-40%, core op margin -25% to -23%) as leased third-party capacity carries the ramp until owned systems come online in Q4.
Structural GAAP haircut: ~$1.13B of customer-warrant assets amortize as contra-revenue for years; the $30M GAAP-vs-core gap is not one-time.
NVIDIA-Groq squeeze on both demand and TSMC supply priority; TSMC single-source dependency, process not portable.
Cash burn: 1H26 operating cash flow -$47.5M with $549M capex, funded by the $6.4B IPO plus a ~$918M working capital loan.
Lockup: ~28M Class A shares tradeable two trading days after the Q2 report (~Aug 14, 2026, per pre-IPO disclosure) - landing on a tape already down ~17% after hours.
catalysts: ~Aug 14, 2026: IPO lockup release (~28M Class A shares).
Q4 2026: owned data centers come online (guided gross-margin inflection); AMD disaggregated inference in production.
Q1 2027: Cerebras on Amazon Bedrock in production.
OpenAI 750MW deployment milestones; proof points against the 'more than triple revenue in 2027' plan and the $25.4B RPO.
pricedIn: Shares closed at $262 on Aug 12 and fell ~17% after hours to ~$215 - roughly $42B market cap (share count approximate), or ~47x the midpoint of FY2026 guided core revenue ($880-890M), down from ~55-60x pre-print. The market paid up for the cloud quadrupling and the $25.4B RPO but balked at 17% core hardware growth and a guided Q3 margin trough. Debate: if 2027 really more than triples to ~$2.7B+, this is ~15x forward core sales for the only proven non-NVIDIA inference platform; if the ramp slips, a UAE-concentrated company burning cash on leased capacity holds a multiple it cannot defend.

scenarios.bear: The ~Aug 14 lockup dumps ~28M shares into a spooked tape; the Q3 margin trough extends into Q4 as owned capacity slips; hardware keeps shrinking; OpenAI consolidates onto NVIDIA/Groq and internal silicon; multiple compresses toward 15-20x core sales (roughly $70-95).
scenarios.base: FY2026 lands at $880-890M with the Q4 owned-capacity margin inflection on schedule; 2027 revenue at least doubles against the RPO; AWS Bedrock broadens the base beyond the UAE; the lockup digests and the stock holds a 35-50x core-sales band (~$160-230).
scenarios.bull: 2027 delivers the guided triple (~$2.7B+) on OpenAI ramp, Bedrock production, and AMD wins; gross margin clears the low-40s on owned data centers; the RPO keeps compounding past $25.4B; the stock reclaims $300 and challenges its $385 opening print.

valPresets.note: Pre-scale company with three public quarters; TTM revenue uses Yahoo's trailing figure. Values the terminal business off a revenue path, horizon FCF margin, and exit multiple.

latestProse: Q2 FY2026 (reported Aug 12 after close). Core revenue $209.9M +103% YoY (GAAP $180.1M +74%), beating the ~$194M guide - and the stock fell ~17% after hours anyway. The mix flipped: core cloud/services $127.7M (+287%) overtook hardware, while core hardware grew just 17% to $82.1M and GAAP hardware fell ~23% after $28M of warrant amortization. Core gross margin 40.6% (+940bps) vs GAAP 14.2%; core operating loss -$33.6M (-16% margin); GAAP net loss $450.5M (-$2.98/sh) on $377M of IPO-quarter stock comp. RPO reached $25.4B. The disclosure that matters most: a ~$1.13B customer-warrant asset amortizes as contra-revenue for years - the GAAP-vs-core revenue gap is structural, the ongoing price of landing OpenAI and the UAE anchors.
guidanceProse: FY2026 raised across the board: core revenue $880-890M (from $855-865M), core gross margin 41-43%, core operating margin -19% to -17%. But Q3 guides sequentially worse - core revenue $214-216M, gross margin 38-40%, operating margin -25% to -23% - because leased third-party capacity carries the ramp until owned, lower-cost systems come online in Q4. AWS Bedrock production lands Q1 2027, AMD disaggregated inference Q4 2026, and management plans to more than triple revenue in 2027 against the $25.4B RPO.
